bib.title: Building Applications with AI Agents, Chapter 4. Tool Use

question: How should tools (local, API-based, plug-in, MCP, stateful, generated) be designed, registered and configured for AI agents?
contributions: Taxonomy of tool types: local, API-based, plug-in, MCP
Foundation models as tool makers and real-time code generation
Tool-choice configuration and a validate/retry/fall back/log flow

Plug-in section describes ChatGPT plug-ins, since retired.

Code listings are partly garbled/truncated in the extraction; the MCP example has bugs (the 'math' server points to MCP_weather_server.py; assistant message lacks a 'content' key in the fallback branch).
practices: Choose precise, narrowly scoped tool names (Local Tools).
Write clear, distinctive descriptions; avoid overlap (Local Tools).
Use local tools for arithmetic, time zones, calendar, maps (Local Tools).
For API tools, plan fallbacks, HTTPS and strong auth, respect rate limits, anonymize user data, consider multiple providers (API-Based Tools).
Register narrow operations rather than execute-arbitrary-SQL; read-only agents get no write rights (Stateful Tools).
If free-form SQL is unavoidable, sanitize, bind parameters or use prepared statements, minimum-privilege DB account (Stateful Tools).
Log every tool invocation and alert on suspicious patterns (Stateful Tools).
Let models draft tool wrappers from OpenAPI specs, run in a sandbox, human review, then CI/CD (Foundation Models as Tool Makers).
Choose tool-choice mode (auto, any/required, none, pinned) to trade flexibility for determinism (Tool Use Configuration).
Validate with jsonschema or Pydantic, retry with backoff, fall back, log everything (Tool Use Configuration).
